title: Federal Reserve Board announces final individual capital requirements for large banks, effective on October 1

source.name: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

summary: The Federal Reserve Board announced final individual capital requirements for large banks following its 2025 stress test, effective October 1, 2025. Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle W. Bowman characterized this as a period of transition as the Board works to reduce year-over-year volatility in stress testing. Capital requirements consist of a 4.5% minimum CET1, a stress capital buffer of at least 2.5%, and potentially a surcharge for systemic institutions. Morgan Stanley's final requirement was pending a reconsideration request, with a decision expected by September 30, 2025. Note: The April 2025 proposal to average stress test results over two years was pending finalization at time of publication.
key_points: Final individual capital requirements for large banks announced, effective October 1, 2025
Requirements informed by 2025 stress test results providing risk-sensitive, forward-looking capital assessment
Minimum capital requirement is 4.5% CET1 for all banks
Stress capital buffer requirement is at least 2.5%, based on stress test results
Largest and most complex banks may also face a capital surcharge updated annually
Morgan Stanley's stress capital buffer requirement is under reconsideration; final decision expected by September 30, 2025
April 2025 proposal to average stress test results over two years would reduce year-over-year volatility if finalized
why_it_matters: Bank capital requirements directly affect how much capital large institutions must hold against potential losses, influencing their ability to pay dividends, buy back shares, and extend credit. These requirements affect bank profitability, risk appetite, and systemic resilience. The ongoing effort to average stress test results across two years aims to reduce procyclical volatility in capital requirements, which would benefit banks' capital planning during stress periods.
macro_context: This announcement is part of the Fed's broader effort to refine its stress testing and capital requirement framework. The timing follows the 2025 stress test cycle and occurs amid ongoing discussions about reducing regulatory volatility for large banks. The policy represents a transitional phase before potential implementation of the stress test averaging methodology.
market_structure_context: This announcement concerns the regulatory capital framework for large banks under stress testing (Dodd-Frank Act Stress Tests / DFAST). Banks below their total capital requirement face automatic restrictions on capital distributions and discretionary bonus payments. The capital requirements combine a 4.5% minimum CET1 floor, a 2.5%+ stress capital buffer derived from stress test losses, and potentially a G-SIB surcharge for the largest institutions. The attached table provides bank-specific requirements.
